_comment: Your sources. access: free | free_signup | paid. rss: feed URL or null. flag: ACT | KNOW | NOTE — this is the SOURCE PRIOR, a nudge for the content classifier, not the final flag. intake: how content arrives. Any source with an rss URL is fetched; feeds verified live 2 Sep 2026.

sources.name: ASIC media releases
sources.note: ASIC retired its RSS feeds. Checked 2 Sep 2026: /rss/media-releases.xml, /newsroom/rss, /feed and /rss.xml all 404. Bookmark-and-check during the weekly sweep.

sources.name: AFCA determinations
sources.note: No working email subscription (newsletter mid-rebuild as of Aug 2026) and no feed — all AFCA feed paths return 403 to automated clients. Bookmark-and-check during weekly sweep: determinations search + media releases page. Determinations are read deliberately, not skimmed — check-the-site is the right intake here, not a fallback.

sources.name: ABS releases
sources.note: ABS retired its site-wide RSS. Checked 2 Sep 2026: /rss.xml, /feed, /statistics/rss all 404. Email alert remains the intake.

sources.name: Treasury consultations
sources.note: treasury.gov.au/rss.xml serves valid RSS but is empty (0 entries as of 2 Sep 2026). Left unconfigured until it carries items; re-probe periodically. Checked again 17 Sep 2026: still empty. ministers.treasury.gov.au/rss.xml does parse, but its newest entry is 11 May 2023 — a valid, stale feed, which is exactly the trap a new source must be probed for before being added.

sources.name: ATO media centre
sources.note: No feed. Checked 17 Sep 2026: /rss/mediareleases.xml, /rss.xml, /feed, /about-ato/media-centre/rss and /newsroom/smallbusiness/rss all 404, and neither the media centre nor the newsroom page advertises one in its HTML. ACT because the ATO both administers tax and regulates SMSFs, so its rulings and guidance change what an adviser does. Bookmark-and-check in the weekly sweep, like ASIC.

sources.name: APRA publications
sources.note: Checked 17 Sep 2026: live, 10 entries, newest that day. Every one of them is a statistics publication — quarterly superannuation, ADI, life, general and private health insurance — so the prior is NOTE, not ACT. This is the data feed, not the enforcement one: APRA's prudential actions and media releases are announced on pages with no feed of their own, and stay bookmark-and-check.

sources.name: Tax Practitioners Board
sources.note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Probed the same day: live, 10 entries, newest that day, recent items covering sanctions-power guidance and registration terminations. ACT because the TPB registers tax (financial) advisers — its terminations and guidance change what an adviser may do, not just what they should know. The only working government feed found in the 17 Sep probe. Watch the volume: it publishes roughly weekly, and an ACT prior puts every item in front of you at every sweep. Known quirk: the feed's description field repeats the title and appends an internal ID, the date and the category before the real text, so teasers read oddly ("...sanctions powers tdenp Thu, 2026-09-17 11:59 Media releases The Treasury..."). The link and the title are correct, which is what an ACT item is read from anyway.

sources.name: AUSTRAC news
sources.note: Added 17 Sep 2026. No feed: /rss.xml, /feed and /news/rss all 404, and the news and media page advertises none in its HTML. Bookmark-and-check in the weekly sweep, like ASIC and the ATO. KNOW rather than ACT because the AML/CTF obligations reach advice practices but rarely demand action in the week they are announced.

sources.name: CSLR
sources.note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The feed parses and carries 10 entries, but the newest was 2 Jul 2026 when probed — a low-volume publisher rather than a stale one, so it is configured rather than bookmarked, with a NOTE prior to match how rarely it speaks. Relevant because the levy and its sustainability are what the Aug 2026 Minister's package was about. If it goes quiet for a year, re-probe before assuming it is broken: a valid stale feed is the trap item 13 records.

sources.note: Public feed carries ~50 current items; newsletter continues in parallel.
